title: Polishing and Releasing My Tiny Geography Game
beats: Polish the game from viewer feedback, add gameplay, try future ideas
Compass needs a maths problem first: which way to face on a globe?
Plane cannot burrow, so straight line is out; need path along surface
Cross centre-to-A with centre-to-B to get plane normal; cross again with A for heading
Writes a test: arrows from many points to a target, checks visually
Compass graphic and code; tests in game flying east then north
Wants a map; wonders what shortest path looks like on a flat map
Slerp between two points drawn on 2D map; straight on equator, curved off it
Names equirectangular and shows other projections with tradeoffs
Chooses a globe instead; Antarctica mesh is bad
Shader reprojection with two sliders; Antarctica split, climbs, reforms at centre
Degrees-to-radians bug makes the view nauseating; fixes it
Path code from the diversion gets reused for the landing arc
Rewrites terrain to one mesh per country; fixes z-fighting and outlines
City lights: reveals iteration count was 10 not 100; shows 0, 10, 200
Glow, star colours, rim lighting each tested with a parameter change
Time of day button; hot air balloons with flag textures
Speed range and boost meter tested by flying
OpenStreetMap Paris test and skywriting idea; asks viewers for thoughts
Menu, release links, score and endless mode

new_moves.name: productive-detour
new_moves.what: Detour explored out of curiosity then explicitly paid off later

new_moves.name: admit-uncertainty-in-parameters
new_moves.what: Shows own parameter error and re-runs to compare

theory: This is a build log, not a lesson. Its teaching value is showing the actual process: test the code, watch it fail, sweep a parameter, then fix. Honest failure and visible sweeps do the work a worked example would.
velocity: Learner model: a stuck student can get a 'write a test and watch it' scene rather than more explanation
Scene builder: parameter-sweep scenes (0, 10, 200) with a slider to show what a number does
Orchestrator: allow a labelled detour and schedule its payoff callback
Voice: playful asides keep a flat rate engaging, but avoid one-sentence maths for novices
quote: Are you excited for some maths? Of course you are!
